 2                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   The 

 3   Senate will come to order.

 5   and join with me as we recite the Pledge of 

 6   Allegiance to our Flag.

 7                (Whereupon, the assemblage recited 

 8   the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

 9                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Today's 

10   invocation will be offered by the Reverend Peter 

11   G. Young, of the Mother Teresa Community here in 

12   Albany.  

13                Father Young.

14                REVEREND YOUNG:   Thank you very 

15   much, Senator.  

16                Today the desire to share in God's 

17   love is exemplified by the two gentlemen that 

18   I'll speak about who are now going with God in 

19   heaven.

20                We want to remember that their 

21   kindness was there to help us when we needed it, 

22   when we were weak, when we were sick or 

23   unfortunate.  Their love for us and for God has 

24   always called upon them to show mercy.  

25                God, by Your love You've made a 


                                                                2121

 1   world where we have become neighbors to each 

 2   other and we are enabled to love one another.  

 3   Grant that we today may too use the Senate to 

 4   strive toward a way of life in keeping with 

 5   God's plan.  

 6                God, you have given us a marvelous 

 7   example in Senator Pisani and in the Senator 

 8   that we have just lost again, Thomas Libous, for 

 9   their service and for their dedication to being 

10   a public servant in the State of New York.  Send 

11   down Your blessing on these Senators who 

12   generously devoted themselves to helping our 

13   New York State citizens.  We pray for these very 

14   dedicated public servants.  

15                My close contemporary friend, Joe 

16   Pisani, we traveled together to open up 

17   19 alcohol treatment centers for the state, and 

18   it was an enjoyable opportunity to be with him 

19   in many of those trips.  

20                We remember the goodness of our 

21   dear friend Thomas Libous, who in '53 went on to 

22   do all of the good work for 14 different terms 

23   in service.  He was a towering legacy -- in the 

24   papers that I've read about him today, they kept 

25   repeating it and repeating it -- for what he did 


                                                                2122

 1   for Broome County, for District 52.  

 2                In that Class of '71, he ran and 

 3   won for the Johnson City High School presidency.  

 4   That was the first time of elected office.  It 

 5   was an amazing kind of thing to hear and to see, 

 6   being born in '53, being able to be the 

 7   dedicated kind of guy that he was.  

 8                We're going to miss him, God.  We 

 9   miss him and we pray that he'll be able to be an 

10   example of dedication to many as he was in the 

11   Transportation Committee, the Alcohol & Drug 

12   Committee, the Mental Health Committee, the 

13   Commerce decision, and all of the kind of 

14   economy he brought again back home for the 

15   Triple Cities.  

16                May we again pray that he'll reach 

17   out and touch us and the many that he especially 

18   had an identification with, the Special 

19   Olympics, and to Fran, his wife, and his son.  

20                May we remember them for the 

21   personal kind of dedication that they've given 

22   to the floor of the Senators of New York State, 

23   and the kind of example they've been dedicated 

24   to be -- a light for us, and a beacon of hope.  

25                Amen.

 1                The Secretary will continue.

 2                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

 3   Resolution Number 5134, by Senator DeFrancisco, 

 4   congratulating the Syracuse University Women's 

 5   Basketball Team upon the occasion of its 

 6   record-breaking season, which led them to the 

 7   first National Collegiate Athletic Association 

 8   (NCAA) Women's Championship game in program 

 9   history.  

10                "WHEREAS, Excellence and success in 

11   competitive sports can be achieved through 

12   strenuous practice, teamwork and a dedicated 

13   coaching staff; and 

14                "WHEREAS, It is the sense of this 

15   Legislative Body to recognize and pay tribute to 

16   those student athletes within our midst who, by 

17   achieving outstanding success in athletic 

18   competition, have inspired and brought great 

19   pride to their college and community; and 

20                "WHEREAS, Athletic competition 

21   enhances the moral and physical development of 

22   the young people of this state, preparing them 

23   for the future by instilling in them the value of 

24   teamwork, encouraging a standard of healthy 

25   living, imparting a desire for success, and by 


                                                                2127

 1   developing a sense of fair play and competition; 

 2   and 

 3                "WHEREAS, Attendant to such concern,  

 4   and in full accord with its long-standing 

 5   traditions, this Legislative Body is justly proud 

 6   to congratulate and recognize the Syracuse 

 7   University Women's Basketball Team upon the 

 8   occasion of its record-breaking season, which led 

 9   them to the first National Collegiate Athletic 

10   Association (NCAA) Women's Championship game in 

11   program history; and 

12                "WHEREAS, Following its historic run 

13   to the NCAA championship game, the Syracuse 

14   University Women's Basketball Team, with an 

15   overall record of 30-8, shot to its highest 

16   ranking in program history in the USA Today 

17   Coaches Poll, reaching No. 3 nationwide; and 

18                "WHEREAS, The Syracuse University 

19   Women's Basketball Team also achieved the most 

20   wins in program history, as well as the program's 

21   first Sweet 16, Elite Eight, Final Four and 

22   NCAA championship game appearances; and 

23                "WHEREAS, On March 20, 2016, the 

24   No. 14/15 Syracuse University Women's Basketball 

25   Team fought its way to the program's first Sweet 


                                                                2128

 1   16 appearance after defeating Albany 76-59 in the 

 2   Carrier Dome; the win marked another 

 3   record-breaking day in a historic season for  

 4   Syracuse, with the team's 27th victory and with 

 5   the senior class earning its 96th win; and 

 6                "WHEREAS, At the Sweet 16 in 

 7   Sioux Falls, South Dakota, the Syracuse 

 8   University Women's Basketball Team upset 

 9   top-seeded South Carolina 80-72 to advance to the 

10   Elite Eight, where it then landed a 89-67 victory 

11   over Tennessee, with the impressive contest 

12   setting yet another program record for the points 

13   scored in an NCAA Tournament game by the Syracuse 

14   University Orange; and 

15                "WHEREAS, Further history was made 

16   when the Syracuse University Women's Basketball 

17   Team hustled its way to the NCAA Tournament final 

18   with a dominant 80-59 victory over the Washington 

19   Huskies at the Final Four in Indianapolis on 

20   April 3rd; the victory placed the program one win  

21   away from a national title and marked the first 

22   30-win season in program history, giving the 2016 

23   Syracuse University Women's Basketball senior 

24   class 99 wins for their collegiate careers; and 

25                "WHEREAS, Though the Syracuse 


                                                                2129

 1   University Women's Basketball Team lost the NCAA 

 2   tournament title to the University of Connecticut 

 3   (UConn), the team played hard, never gave up, and 

 4   kept their heads high; and 

 5                "WHEREAS, The outstanding athletic 

 6   talent, teamwork and sportsmanship displayed by 

 7   the Syracuse University Women's Basketball Team 

 8   is due in great part to the skilled and 

 9   supportive efforts of Head Coach Quentin 

10   Hillsman, Associate Head Coach Vonn Read, 

11   Assistant Coach Tammi Reiss, Assistant Coach 

12   Cedric Solice, and Multimedia and Technology 

13   Director Ryan Nichols; and 

14                "WHEREAS, Throughout the season, the 

15   support of fans within both the Syracuse  

16   University and Central New York communities 

17   significantly grew in enthusiasm; and 

18                "WHEREAS, Members of the Syracuse 

19   University Women's Basketball Team rallied  

20   behind one another in establishing a sisterhood 

21   of athletic ability, good sportsmanship, honor 

22   and scholarship, while demonstrating that these 

23   team players are of the highest caliber, while 

24   contributing to the spirit of excellence that is 

25   a tradition of their university; now, therefore, 


                                                                2130

 1   be it 

 2                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

 3   Body pause in its deliberations to congratulate  

 4   the Syracuse University Women's Basketball Team;  

 5   its outstanding  members:  Alexis Peterson, Julia 

 6   Chandler, Maggie Morrison, Jade Phillips, 

 7   Isabella Slim, Cornelia Fondren, Aliyah Parris,  

 8   Brianna Butler, Savannah Crocetti, Brittney 

 9   Sykes, Danielle Minott, Taylor Ford, Brandi  

10   Fowler, Davida Dale, Abby Grant, Briana Day, and 

11   Bria Day; and Head Coach Quentin Hillsman, 

12   Associate Head Coach Vonn Read, Assistant Coach 

13   Tammi Reiss, Assistant Coach Cedric Solice, and 

14   Multimedia and Technology Director Ryan Nichols, 

15   on their outstanding season and overall team 

16   record; and be it further 

17                "RESOLVED, That copies of this  

18   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to 

19   members of the Syracuse University Women's 

20   Basketball Team, and the aforementioned coaches 

21   and staff."

22                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

23   DeFrancisco.

24                SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:   Yes, I'm 

25   probably more excited that they're here than they 


                                                                2131

 1   are, quite frankly, because I watched with great 

 2   interest as this team made history week after 

 3   week after week.  It hadn't been -- in the recent 

 4   past, it's been difficult to get in, first of 

 5   all, to get in the tournament and then to get in 

 6   some of the steps of the tournament.  

 7                And so when they got into the Sweet 

 8   16 this year, that was a major accomplishment, at 

 9   least most of us thought.  It wasn't major to 

10   them, because they knew what they had on the team 

11   and they knew they were going further.  Then the 

12   Elite Eight.  And finally, the Final Four, where 

13   they got to the final game.  It was so exciting, 

14   so unbelievable.  

15                When they were in my office earlier 

16   for a brief lunch, I compared them to the days of 

17   Syracuse men's basketball when Dave Bing brought 

18   the Syracuse University team into a different 

19   era, a nationally known era, a nationally 

20   recognized team.  And this is what's really 

21   happening:  We're experiencing history right now.

22                We are extremely proud of all the 

23   players -- and I'm not going to read all of them 

24   off.  But Coach Quentin Hillsman, who is an 

25   animal -- you watch him on the sideline, you 


                                                                2132

 1   think he needs a tranquilizer.  But he obviously 

 2   knows how to motivate his players, and he's a 

 3   pretty aggressive guy, and I like those kind of 

 4   guys and gals.  

 5                So it's an amazing accomplishment.  

 6   I'm just so happy that they were able to be here 

 7   to be honored.  And they're going to be here next 

 8   year to be honored as the national champions.  

 9                So I just thought we'd give them a 

10   preview of what it's like to come, and maybe 

11   we'll have something better for lunch next year.  

12                (Laughter.)

14   for being here.

16   college and pro football Hall of Fame

19   room.  He was pretty good too.

20                (Laughter.)

21                SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:   He was pretty 

22   good too.

23                So thank you, Mr. President.  And 

24   congratulations to all of you.

25                (Extended applause.)

 1   Mr. President.

 2                You know, I feel bad that the young 

 3   ladies and the coaches had left, because there's 

 4   two things that I was going to say in relation to 

 5   that resolution.  

 6                First is that we oftentimes focus on 

 7   the things that are great theater and great 

 8   media, but not a lot of people talk about what a 

 9   fantastic academic university Syracuse is.  

10                So I think their first reputation 

11   lies in that area, and all the other stuff is 

12   icing on top of the cake that was already 

13   properly and well-baked.

14                The second thing is I was going to 

15   tell those young ladies that they should never 

16   play basketball with DeFrancisco, because I've 

17   played with him and he's a great shooter, but he 

18   stinks at passing.  

19                (Laughter.)

20                SENATOR FLANAGAN:   And he takes 

21   great pride in that.

22                So I rise for a very important point 

23   to make.  And yesterday, yesterday was a very sad 

24   day for the people of the great State of 

25   New York, for the people of the Southern Tier, 


                                                                2139

 1   for the Libous family, for the Senate family, and 

 2   for all the people who knew and had great 

 3   affection and love for Tom Libous.  

 4                Now, we are going to have a separate 

 5   time and place -- I've spoken to Senator 

 6   Gianaris -- let me be clear.  On May 17th we are 

 7   going to have a proper and more formal resolution 

 8   advanced in honor of Senator Libous, in large 

 9   part so we can pay respect to him while his 

10   family is here.  So at that time I would suggest 

11   that would be the appropriate venue and moment 

12   for people to offer their thoughts, and I'm sure 

13   there are going to be plenty of them.

14                But what I wanted to do today was 

15   concise, clear and simple.  The Senate is a 

16   family, and no matter how long you've been here, 

17   you find that out pretty quickly.  Tom Libous was 

18   a fantastic public servant.  He was so proud of 

19   representing his community.  And let's be clear:  

20   Senator Akshar has a very, very difficult job.  

21   Tom was a giant in Broome County and Senate 

22   District 52.  And the people of those 

23   communities, I'm not sure that they ever truly 

24   appreciated the depth and scope and breadth of 

25   his experience and his talent.


                                                                2140

 1                He was clever, he was smart.  He 

 2   could be a pain in the neck sometimes, which 

 3   worked to our benefit.  But he was a born and 

 4   bred New Yorker.  He was so eminently proud of 

 5   being a public servant, being a New York State 

 6   Senator, being from the Southern Tier and serving 

 7   in this house.  And he got a chance to sit in the 

 8   seat that Senator DeFrancisco is in now, had an 

 9   excellent working relationship -- with an 

10   occasional bump in the road -- with Senator 

11   Gianaris, but on the whole they developed a very 

12   collegial, strong working relationship.  

13                So I learned something today that I 

14   think is very useful.  But before I do that, I 

15   just want to recognize, you know, you try and 

16   find a silver lining in things that go on in 

17   life.  Everybody knows what a diehard fan Tom 

18   Libous was of the New York Mets.  All right?  I'm 

19   a Yankees fan, Lanza is a Yankees fan, Gianaris 

20   is a Mets fan, Robach is a Mets fan, so we have 

21   our rivalries.  But we are New Yorkers first and 

22   foremost.  

23                So I checked -- and everybody reads 

24   the stuff in the media.  I just want to make sure 

25   I'm giving my numbers out exactly correct.  Much

 1   to my chagrin, the Yankees are now 8 and 16.

 2                (Laughter.)

 3                SENATOR FLANAGAN:   You know, it 

 4   breaks my heart.

 6   blessing for Tom Libous -- the Mets are 16 and 9.

 8   about this, he gets to watch the Mets now; he 

 9   just has better seats.

10                Now, we learn from the people we 

11   work with.  And there's a very talented young 

12   lady on our staff who's seated here right now who 

13   gave me good advice this morning.  Sometimes we 

14   get too solemn on occasions about life when what

17   of silence to acknowledge the solemnity of 

18   Senator Libous's passing, we're going to veer
